pr.body:
Changes:
- Initializes unified storage when the `ResourceServer` is created, instead of doing it inside the first gRPC call it receives. This was causing context cancelled errors since the index takes too long to build within the context of the gRPC call.
- Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down.
- Improves index build speed using finer grain locking when writing the index cache. We were locking the whole `BuildIndex` function, which was slowing things down when building many namespaces with high concurrency.

Notes for reviewer:
- Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?
pr.title: Unified Storage: Init at startup, fix traces, and speed up indexing

raw_findings.body: The only integration test exercising the storage server module (which now eagerly initializes unified storage at construction time, per this PR) is no longer executed against postgres, so a postgres-specific regression from the init-order/timing changes in this PR would go undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent loss of CI coverage for the postgres backend path introduced/affected by this PR.
raw_findings.impact: The only integration test exercising the storage server module (which now eagerly initializes unified storage at construction time, per this PR) is no longer executed against postgres, so a postgres-specific regression from the init-order/timing changes in this PR would go undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: Test disabled via unconditional skip with only a TODO comment rather than addressing the underlying incompatibility.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Investigate and fix the postgres-specific failure (likely related to the new synchronous Init() during server construction) instead of skipping the test, or add a tracking issue reference and a narrower regression test that still exercises the changed startup path on postgres.
raw_findings.title: Postgres integration test skipped instead of fixed, silently dropping coverage

raw_findings.body: The identical error message 'error initializing resource server' is logged twice (once inside Init()'s once.Do block, once here), producing confusing duplicate log entries during startup failure diagnosis.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Noisy/duplicated log output that can mislead operators investigating startup failures.
raw_findings.impact: The identical error message 'error initializing resource server' is logged twice (once inside Init()'s once.Do block, once here), producing confusing duplicate log entries during startup failure diagnosis.
raw_findings.root_cause: New error-handling block added after the newly-introduced s.Init(ctx) call duplicates logging already performed inside Init().
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove this redundant s.log.Error call in NewResourceServer since Init() already logs the same error internally, and just propagate the returned error.
raw_findings.title: Duplicate error logging when NewResourceServer's eager Init fails
raw_findings.trigger: NewResourceServer is called and s.Init(ctx) returns a non-nil error (lifecycle.Init, search.init, or initWatcher failure).

raw_findings.body: Both goroutines can concurrently call bleve.New(dir, mapper) against the identical on-disk directory (file-backed index branch), risking corrupted or unusable index files, and the final unsynchronized-until-the-end b.cache[key]=idx assignment becomes a last-writer-wins race that silently discards one of the built indexes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: On-disk bleve index corruption, open errors, or wasted/duplicated index builds under concurrent load for the same namespaced resource.
raw_findings.impact: Both goroutines can concurrently call bleve.New(dir, mapper) against the identical on-disk directory (file-backed index branch), risking corrupted or unusable index files, and the final unsynchronized-until-the-end b.cache[key]=idx assignment becomes a last-writer-wins race that silently discards one of the built indexes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The coarse cacheMu.Lock()/Unlock() that previously serialized the entire BuildIndex call (and, as a side effect, prevented concurrent duplicate builds for the same key) was deleted and replaced only with a narrow lock around the final cache map write, leaving no protection against concurrent same-key builds.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Introduce per-key locking (e.g., a mutex/singleflight keyed by NamespacedResource) to serialize concurrent builds for the same key, while keeping the newly added fine-grained lock only for protecting the shared cache map access across different keys.
raw_findings.title: Removing whole-function lock in BuildIndex allows concurrent same-key builds to race on disk
raw_findings.trigger: Two concurrent calls reach BuildIndex for the same NamespacedResource key (e.g., concurrent Search/getOrCreateIndex calls for a namespace not yet cached, or a rebuild racing with the initial build) now that the whole-function lock guarding all builds has been removed.

raw_findings.body: Concurrent unsynchronized access between TotalDocs()'s map iteration and BuildIndex()'s map write can trigger a Go runtime 'concurrent map read and map write' fatal error, crashing the process during startup, or yield an inconsistent document count in the log.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Potential fatal runtime panic ('concurrent map read and map write') or inaccurate document counts reported at startup.
raw_findings.impact: Concurrent unsynchronized access between TotalDocs()'s map iteration and BuildIndex()'s map write can trigger a Go runtime 'concurrent map read and map write' fatal error, crashing the process during startup, or yield an inconsistent document count in the log.
raw_findings.root_cause: A new logging call reading TotalDocs() was added right after starting a concurrent goroutine capable of mutating the same underlying map, while TotalDocs() itself performs no locking.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Have TotalDocs() acquire cacheMu.RLock() before iterating the cache map, or move/skip this log statement so it does not race with the just-started event-handling goroutine.
raw_findings.title: New startup log line calls unsynchronized TotalDocs() concurrently with index-building goroutine
raw_findings.trigger: Immediately after starting the async event-handling goroutine (go func() { for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } }()), which can trigger new BuildIndex calls that write to bleveBackend.cache, this newly-added log line calls s.search.TotalDocs(), which iterates the same cache map without acquiring cacheMu.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds a skip for postgres with a TODO comment, but this is a pre-existing test that was already skipping sqlite. finding.trigger: NewResourceServer is called and s.Init(ctx) returns a non-nil error (lifecycle.Init, search.init, or initWatcher failure).
finding.verifier_reason: The claim of duplicate logging is incorrect. Looking at server.go lines 293-318, Init() logs 'error initializing resource server' only when s.initErr != nil at line 314. The new code at lines 258-262 logs the same message when Init() returns an error. However, Init() uses sync.Once, so the error is logged once inside once.Do, then returned. The caller then logs again - but this is standard Go error handling pattern (log at boundary), not a defect. The messages also differ: Init logs s.initErr, caller logs err.

finding.verifier_reason: The candidate cites LEFT side line 88 showing the lock being REMOVED, but the patch shows this is the OLD code (lines L88-L89 with minus signs indicate deletion). finding.body: Concurrent unsynchronized access between TotalDocs()'s map iteration and BuildIndex()'s map write can trigger a Go runtime 'concurrent map read and map write' fatal error, crashing the process during startup, or yield an inconsistent document count in the log.
finding.failure_mode: Potential fatal runtime panic ('concurrent map read and map write') or inaccurate document counts reported at startup.
finding.impact: Concurrent unsynchronized access between TotalDocs()'s map iteration and BuildIndex()'s map write can trigger a Go runtime 'concurrent map read and map write' fatal error, crashing the process during startup, or yield an inconsistent document count in the log.
finding.root_cause: A new logging call reading TotalDocs() was added right after starting a concurrent goroutine capable of mutating the same underlying map, while TotalDocs() itself performs no locking.
finding.suggested_fix: Have TotalDocs() acquire cacheMu.RLock() before iterating the cache map, or move/skip this log statement so it does not race with the just-started event-handling goroutine.
finding.title: New startup log line calls unsynchronized TotalDocs() concurrently with index-building goroutine
finding.trigger: Immediately after starting the async event-handling goroutine (go func() { for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } }()), which can trigger new BuildIndex calls that write to bleveBackend.cache, this newly-added log line calls s.search.TotalDocs(), which iterates the same cache map without acquiring cacheMu.
finding.verifier_reason: The candidate claims TotalDocs() races with the goroutine started at line 207. However, examining the code flow: the goroutine reads from 'events' channel (line 209), then calls handleEvent. The TotalDocs() call at line 216 happens AFTER the goroutine starts but the goroutine blocks on channel receive. The race would require handleEvent to call BuildIndex before TotalDocs completes. While theoretically possible, the candidate provides no evidence that TotalDocs lacks synchronization - GetIndex at bleve.go:60-62 shows RLock is used. The claim about cacheMu not being held in TotalDocs is unverified from available context.
